state.goal: Keep source-owned typed Contracts usable for ordinary SaaS records with compact authoring, one canonical equality/encoding primitive, no reserved business-field workaround, coherent permissions/order/failure/rollback/recovery. This is an implementation representation choice, not permission to redesign Can.
state.required_outcome: A declared Contract {kind:text,model:text,id:text,version:int} with kind=ref compares and encodes ALL business fields, including version. A declared Model leaf instead compares Model/id identity and ignores concurrency version. Nested Contracts/aliases/arrays/unions, plain source constructors, decoded inputs, locked snapshots, hydration and transport must agree. No extra source syntax. Malformed tagged values outside proven Contract positions must still fail; field spelling alone never grants reference authority. Native reference resolution remains genuine and only demanded by the existing lazy comparison/encoding order; do not eagerly walk values or swallow failures.
verified_context: Values validateContractValue(schema-core.ts700) accepts any declared kind field and returns frozen plain object. equalValue typeId is currently an opaque label; its runtime dispatch checks isRecordRef before Contract fields, then rejects malformed known kind tags. Consequently ref-shaped Contract can ignore business fields, or ordinary kind=ref Contract throws. encodeValue has the same runtime shape collision in encodeDynamic/encodeNominal, so equality-only repair is incomplete.

Current equalValue has optional native reference resolver as fourth argument; encodeValue has optional demanded path-aware native reference resolver as third. Existing untyped malformed {kind:file} and {kind:ref,id:empty} controls must remain refusals. No value-type interpretation creates a native reference grant.

State locked field comparison now has exact checked receiving schema through a private actual-field association; CF encodeCanonicalField already receives loaded owning schema, but currently validates after potentially lossy encoding. CF stdlib equality drops c and passes only nativeRecordReference; generated equality in normal and hook code carries type string, no schema. Source-owned module/operation schema delivery must therefore be completed if dispatch uses schemas, without global mutable name lookup.

Compiler Contract constructions currently lower to plain JS object literals. CF scenario hydration reconstructs Contract containers with Object.freeze(Object.fromEntries(...)); makeUnionValue copies its value; State frozen() uses structuredClone. None preserves a new WeakMap identity automatically. Wire transport must always reacquire type from the exact receiving schema. Adding a validation-only brand is insufficient.

representation.instructions: Choose between these two fully completed alternatives on equal acceptance criteria: correct Contract business fields, Model identity, lazy genuine references, unchanged failures and total ongoing complexity.

criteria.schema_dispatch: Give the existing equality and encoder an optional authenticated owning schema/type context, then structurally interpret only its proved Contract positions. Preserve type-directed recursion and reference-leaf semantics; complete source-owned codegen/native plumbing for ordinary and hook calls. Retain existing fallback behavior outside such context. No duplicated equality API, global registry or source spelling change is required, but more consumers must forward the schema.
criteria.private_provenance: Use nonpublic Contract provenance acquired from typed source construction and validation, recognized by the current equality and encoder before ambiguous tags. Complete explicit propagation or reconstruction through hydrated containers, unions, structured cloning and received wire values. Preserve unmarked malformed-value controls and business wire bytes. No schema must be passed at each comparison, but all value-producing/copying boundaries must maintain the mark.
